title: SYSK Selects: Subways: HUH! What are they good for?
summary: SYSK Selects rerun of the 2012 episode on subways. The hosts open with banter about New York subway confusion, then trace subway history: London's Underground (1863), Paris's Metro, and New York's subway (1904) following the Industrial Revolution and urban crowding, and the horse-drawn omnibus and horse manure problem that pushed transit underground. They cover construction methods including cut-and-cover, the New Austrian tunneling method, tunnel boring machines, dealing with aquifers and rivers using compressed air and caisson-style pods, and ground freezing with calcium chloride. Other topics include the abandoned City Hall station loop on the 6 train, Marta in Atlanta, automated trains, the geometry train that checks track alignment, third rail power, subway car lifespan and disposal at sea, the Coney Island shop, subway ridership rankings, subways as air-raid shelters, the Tokyo sarin attack and 7/7 London bombings, and 9/11 damage to a station. The episode ends with listener mail from Monique about her relationship and the show.

entities.name: The Devil in the White City

segments.title: Rerun introduction and opening banter
segments.summary: Chuck introduces this Selects episode from 2012 and the hosts banter about the A Train song and the difficulty of reading the New York subway map.

segments.title: Subway systems by city and the Industrial Revolution
segments.summary: The hosts compare subway systems in London, Paris and New York and note that the London Underground opened in 1863, the Paris Metro in 1900 and New York in 1904, tied to Industrial Revolution urban growth.

segments.title: Horse-drawn transit and the move underground
segments.summary: Above-ground transit used horses and omnibuses, creating heavy manure problems, which pushed cities to build underground transit.

segments.title: Tunneling challenges and tunnel boring machines
segments.summary: Early tunnels were dug by hand with picks, shovels and dynamite, while modern tunnel boring machines crush rock and support the tunnel. Bedrock, injuries and deaths during New York construction are discussed.

segments.title: Cut and cover and New Austrian tunneling
segments.summary: The hosts describe cut-and-cover construction, where streets are dug up, supported with pilings and beams, and rebuilt, and mention the New Austrian tunneling method as a collection of techniques.

segments.title: Obstacles, utility rerouting, and water hazards
segments.summary: Utility lines are rerouted or hung from beams, unmapped pipes are found, and aquifers and rivers pose danger. Paris used compressed air pods and calcium chloride to freeze mud, and Brooklyn Bridge workers got the bends.

segments.title: Underground curiosities and the abandoned City Hall station
segments.summary: Paris quarries and catacombs, San Francisco Bay cut-and-cover tunnel, and the abandoned City Hall station reached by the 6 train loop, which is no longer open to riders.

segments.title: Automated trains, signals, MARTA, and the geometry train
segments.summary: Automated driverless trains, signal and speed limit systems, MARTA in Atlanta, and the geometry train that measures track alignment and extinguishes fires.

segments.title: Power, fares, ridership, and subway history in war and attacks
segments.summary: Third rail power, fare recovery in New York, subway car lifespan and disposal at sea, Coney Island shop, ridership rankings, subways as air-raid shelters, the Tokyo sarin attack, 7/7 London bombings, and 9/11 damage.

segments.title: Listener mail from Monique and outro
segments.summary: Monique writes about her and Nathan's anniversary, how the show brought them together, and the hosts sign off with contact information.
